nodes.summary: Let $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ be the closed square and $\partial I^2$ its boundary. $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ is the subgroup of the group of homeomorphisms of $I^2$ consisting of those homeomorphisms $h$ with $h(x) = x$ for every $x \in \partial I^2$.
nodes.title: Boundary-fixing homeomorphisms of the square

nodes.summary: Let $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ be the closed square, a model of the closed disc, and let $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ be the group of homeomorphisms of $I^2$ that fix every point of the boundary $\partial I^2$. There is no linear order $\le$ on $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c$; that is, this group is not right-orderable.
nodes.title: Boundary-fixing homeomorphisms of the disc are not right-orderable

nodes.summary: The proposition (Kourovka Problem 17.20, G. M. Bergman, for the closed disc) that the group $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ of homeomorphisms of the closed square $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, a model of the closed disc, that fix the boundary $\partial I^2$ pointwise is right-orderable: it carries a linear order $\le$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c$.
nodes.title: Right-orderability of the boundary-fixing homeomorphisms of the disc

nodes.summary: The right orders of `G`: linear orders (as relations) invariant under right multiplication.
nodes.title: Right orders of a group

nodes.summary: The boundary $\partial I^2$ of the closed square $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ is the set of points $(x, y) \in I^2$ with $x = 0$, $x = 1$, $y = 0$ or $y = 1$.
nodes.title: Boundary of the square

nodes.summary: The closed square $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, the product of two copies of the unit interval, used as a model of the closed disc.
nodes.title: The closed square

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
